vit-xao-rau-ram.name: Duck Stir-Fried with Vietnamese Coriander
aliases: Vietnamese Duck Stir-Fry with Rau Ram
vit-xao-rau-ram.description: Small pieces of duck are cooked through with aromatic Vietnamese coriander, scallion, garlic, and a little chili. This savory dish pairs well with hot rice and cucumber.
vit-xao-rau-ram.finished_dish: The duck is browned and fully cooked, coated in seasoning; the Vietnamese coriander remains fragrant and green.
vit-xao-rau-ram.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice or bread, finishing with fresh Vietnamese coriander and scallion.
tips: Pat the duck dry after rinsing so it sears instead of steaming.
Cut the duck into even pieces and cook in batches if the pan is crowded.
Cook until the thickest pieces are fully done; a food thermometer can be used to check for about 74°C.
vit-xao-rau-ram.image_alt: Vietnamese duck stir-fried with rau ram, scallion, and chili, served on a ceramic plate. Bếp Việt transparent-background illustration.

ingredients.name: Duck meat
ingredients.notes: Use boneless thigh or breast with skin; cut into small even pieces.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese coriander (rau ram)
ingredients.notes: Pick the leaves, rinse, and reserve a little for garnish.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Use for the marinade and final seasoning.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add for a brief covered cook so the duck cooks evenly.

preparation_steps: Rub the duck lightly with salt, rinse, and pat very dry. Remove bones if needed and cut into even pieces.
Marinate with shallot, garlic, fish sauce, and pepper for 20 minutes. Pick and rinse the herbs; cut the scallion and chili.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and sear the duck in batches until browned on the edges.
Return all the duck to the pan, add water, cover, and cook over medium heat for about 12–15 minutes until fully cooked. Uncover, stir, and reduce the liquid.
Add sugar and taste. Toss in the Vietnamese coriander, scallion, and chili for 30–45 seconds, just until fragrant.
vit-xao-rau-ram.serving_basis: A four-person portion prepared by Bếp Việt for a Vietnamese family meal.
vit-xao-rau-ram.time_note: About 65 minutes including a 20-minute marinating period; cooking time depends on piece size and pan heat.
vit-xao-rau-ram.media_alt_text: Vietnamese duck stir-fried with rau ram, scallion, and chili, served on a ceramic plate. Bếp Việt transparent-background illustration.
keywords: Vietnamese Duck Stir-Fry with Rau Ram

canh-ca-khoai-la-giang.name: Whiting Soup with Lá Giang Sour Leaves
aliases: Vietnamese Whiting and Sour Leaf Soup
Canh Chua with Whiting and Lá Giang
canh-ca-khoai-la-giang.description: Tender whiting is simmered with sour lá giang leaves, tomato, and pineapple. The light, tangy broth is served hot with a family meal.
canh-ca-khoai-la-giang.finished_dish: The pale broth is gently sour; the whiting is just cooked and the soup is fragrant with lá giang and fresh herbs.
canh-ca-khoai-la-giang.serving: Ladle the fish gently into a bowl, add hot broth and herbs, and serve with steamed rice.
tips: Whiting is delicate; add it after the broth boils and avoid stirring while it cooks.
Bruise the sour leaves lightly, then taste before adding more seasoning.
Choose fresh fish, clean it carefully, and keep it chilled until cooking.
search_terms: Vietnamese fish and sour leaf soup
canh-ca-khoai-la-giang.image_alt: Vietnamese whiting soup with lá giang, tomato, pineapple, and rice paddy herbs. Bếp Việt transparent-background illustration.

ingredients.name: Whiting
ingredients.notes: Clean, cut into short sections, and drain.

ingredients.name: Pineapple
ingredients.notes: Peel, remove the eyes, and cut into pieces.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balance the sourness of the leaves.

preparation_steps: Clean the whiting, cut it into short sections, and drain. Rinse and lightly bruise the lá giang leaves.
Cut the pineapple and tomatoes; chop the shallot, garlic, rau om, and sawtooth coriander.
cooking_steps: Sauté the shallot and garlic in oil. Add tomatoes and cook until just softened, then add water and pineapple.
When the broth boils, add the lá giang and seasonings. Simmer briefly, then taste for a balanced sour-salty-sweet flavor.
Add the whiting and simmer gently until it is just cooked and the broth returns to a boil. Do not stir vigorously. Turn off the heat and finish with herbs and optional chili.
canh-ca-khoai-la-giang.serving_basis: A four-person portion prepared by Bếp Việt for a Vietnamese family meal.
canh-ca-khoai-la-giang.time_note: About 30 minutes including preparation and cooking; the delicate fish cooks quickly.
canh-ca-khoai-la-giang.media_alt_text: Vietnamese whiting soup with lá giang, tomato, pineapple, and rice paddy herbs. Bếp Việt transparent-background illustration.
keywords: Whiting Soup with Lá Giang Sour Leaves

goi-uc-ga-rau-lang.name: Chicken Breast and Sweet Potato Leaf Salad
aliases: Vietnamese Chicken and Sweet Potato Leaf Salad
goi-uc-ga-rau-lang.description: Shredded chicken is mixed with briefly boiled sweet potato leaves, thin onion, Vietnamese coriander, and a lime fish-sauce dressing. Tangy and fresh, it adds greens to a family meal.
goi-uc-ga-rau-lang.finished_dish: The chicken is tender and shredded, the leaves are green and soft, and the light dressing coats the salad without pooling.
goi-uc-ga-rau-lang.serving: Toss shortly before serving, arrange on a wide plate, and enjoy with plain rice porridge or as a salad course.
tips: Poach the chicken gently until fully cooked, then rest it briefly before shredding to help keep it moist.
Drain the sweet potato leaves thoroughly so the salad does not turn watery.
Start with a little dressing, taste, and add more gradually to balance sour, salty, and sweet notes.
search_terms: chicken breast and sweet potato leaf salad
Vietnamese chicken and rau lang salad
goi-uc-ga-rau-lang.image_alt: Vietnamese chicken and sweet potato leaf salad with onion, Vietnamese coriander, and chili. Bếp Việt transparent-background illustration.

ingredients.name: Chicken breast
ingredients.notes: Rinse and leave whole for poaching.

ingredients.name: Tender sweet potato leaves and shoots
ingredients.notes: Remove fibrous stems and rinse well.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For poaching the chicken and boiling the greens separately.

preparation_steps: Rub the chicken with a little salt, rinse, and drain. Pick the sweet potato leaves; slice the onion and chop the rau ram. Soak the onion briefly in cold water, then drain.
Stir together the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, 30 ml water, garlic, and chili until the sugar dissolves.
cooking_steps: Poach the chicken gently until fully cooked. Remove it, let it cool slightly, and shred into strips.
Bring fresh water with a little salt to a boil. Cook the sweet potato leaves for 3–4 minutes until tender, then drain thoroughly and cut into short lengths.
Toss the chicken, leaves, onion, and rau ram with just enough dressing. Rest for about 5 minutes, taste, and arrange on a serving plate.
goi-uc-ga-rau-lang.serving_basis: A four-person portion prepared by Bếp Việt for a Vietnamese family meal.
goi-uc-ga-rau-lang.time_note: About 50 minutes including preparation, cooking, and a short rest; chicken time depends on thickness.
goi-uc-ga-rau-lang.media_alt_text: Vietnamese chicken and sweet potato leaf salad with onion, Vietnamese coriander, and chili. Bếp Việt transparent-background illustration.
keywords: Chicken Breast and Sweet Potato Leaf Salad

rau-nhut-xao-toi.name: Garlic Stir-Fried Water Mimosa
rau-nhut-xao-toi.description: Young water mimosa stems are quickly stir-fried with fragrant garlic and lightly seasoned to keep their crisp, fresh flavor. This plant-based Southern Vietnamese side pairs well with steamed rice.
rau-nhut-xao-toi.finished_dish: The greens stay bright and crisp-tender, with golden fragrant garlic and little excess liquid.
rau-nhut-xao-toi.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and a braised or simmered main dish.
tips: Remove the white spongy floats and fibrous stems, keeping the tender parts so the greens are not tough.
Drain the greens well and use a wide pan over high heat to cook them quickly with less water.
Use a plant-based seasoning and taste lightly once the greens are just cooked.
rau-nhut-xao-toi.image_alt: Garlic stir-fried water mimosa with crisp green stems and a little red chili. Bếp Việt transparent-background illustration.

ingredients.name: Water mimosa
ingredients.notes: Remove the white floats and tough stems; cut into serving lengths.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For sautéing the garlic and greens.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Choose a product labeled plant-based; season gradually.

preparation_steps: Remove the white spongy floats and old leaves, rinse the water mimosa several times, cut into about 5 cm lengths, and drain well.
Peel and chop the garlic; slice the chili if using.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and sauté the garlic until fragrant and lightly golden.
Add the water mimosa and toss quickly over high heat for about 3–5 minutes, until just tender but still crisp.
Season gradually with vegetarian seasoning powder and salt; add optional chili, toss for another 30 seconds, and turn off the heat.
rau-nhut-xao-toi.serving_basis: A four-person portion prepared by Bếp Việt for a Vietnamese family meal.
rau-nhut-xao-toi.time_note: About 18 minutes including preparation and cooking; adjust for the tenderness of the greens and pan size.
rau-nhut-xao-toi.media_alt_text: Garlic stir-fried water mimosa with crisp green stems and a little red chili. Bếp Việt transparent-background illustration.

mong-toi-xao-thit-bam.name: Malabar Spinach Stir-Fried with Minced Pork
aliases: Vietnamese Malabar Spinach with Minced Pork
Rau Mong Toi with Minced Pork
mong-toi-xao-thit-bam.description: Tender Malabar spinach is stir-fried with minced pork and fragrant garlic. Lightly savory and quick to prepare, it pairs well with rice in a family meal.
mong-toi-xao-thit-bam.finished_dish: The minced pork is fully cooked and seasoned; the Malabar spinach is tender, green, and lightly coated with pan juices.
mong-toi-xao-thit-bam.serving: Serve hot in a shallow dish with a little pan juice and steamed rice.
tips: Discard yellow leaves and wash the greens well; drain them so the pan does not become watery.
Cook the minced pork through before adding the greens; Malabar spinach softens quickly, so avoid overcooking.
Season with a light hand and taste again after the greens release their juices.
search_terms: Malabar spinach stir-fried with minced pork
rau mong toi with ground pork
mong-toi-xao-thit-bam.image_alt: Malabar spinach stir-fried with minced pork and garlic, served on a ceramic plate. Bếp Việt transparent-background illustration.

ingredients.name: Malabar spinach
ingredients.notes: Pick the tender leaves and stems, rinse, drain, and cut into lengths.

ingredients.name: Ground pork
ingredients.notes: Choose shoulder with a little fat so the dish stays moist.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For sautéing the garlic and pork.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Use for the marinade and final seasoning.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the greens only if needed.

preparation_steps: Discard wilted leaves and tough stems. Rinse the Malabar spinach, drain, and cut into serving lengths.
Marinate the pork with half the fish sauce, pepper, and sugar for about 10 minutes; peel and crush the garlic.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil, sauté the garlic until fragrant, then add the minced pork and break it up. Cook fully.
Add the Malabar spinach and toss briefly until the leaves wilt and release a little liquid.
Add the remaining fish sauce and salt if needed. Toss for another 1–2 minutes and turn off the heat as soon as the greens are tender.
mong-toi-xao-thit-bam.serving_basis: A four-person portion prepared by Bếp Việt for a Vietnamese family meal.
mong-toi-xao-thit-bam.time_note: About 34 minutes including preparation, a short marinade, and cooking; do not overcook the greens.
